f3_program: collection("jace.trip.driving_distances", "distance", "jace.trip", source("Jace drives for 4 hours straight, take a 30-minute break, and then drives for another 9 hours straight"))
member("jace.trip.driving_distances", "jace.trip.first_drive.distance", source("Jace drives for 4 hours straight"))
member("jace.trip.driving_distances", "jace.trip.second_drive.distance", source("drives for another 9 hours straight"))
observe(at("jace.driving.speed", "current"), 60, "mile_per_hour", source("Jace drives 60 miles per hour"))
observe(at("jace.trip.first_drive.duration", "current"), 4, "hour", source("Jace drives for 4 hours straight"))
observe(at("jace.trip.break.duration", "current"), 30, "minute", source("a 30-minute break"))
observe(at("jace.trip.second_drive.duration", "current"), 9, "hour", source("drives for another 9 hours straight"))

rate_relation("jace.trip.first_drive.distance", at("jace.driving.speed", "current"), at("jace.trip.first_drive.duration", "current"), source("Jace drives 60 miles per hour. If Jace drives for 4 hours straight"))

rate_relation("jace.trip.second_drive.distance", at("jace.driving.speed", "current"), at("jace.trip.second_drive.duration", "current"), source("Jace drives 60 miles per hour. If Jace drives for 4 hours straight, take a 30-minute break, and then drives for another 9 hours straight"))
query("sum", "jace.trip.driving_distances", "current")
assumptions: The stated driving speed applies to both driving intervals.

f3_program: collection("friends.blue_marble_counts", "blue_marble_count", "mary_and_friends", source("Mary and her two friends came up with the idea of collecting marbles each day"))
member("friends.blue_marble_counts", "mary.marbles.blue.count", source("Mary collected twice as many red marbles as Jenny and half the number of blue marbles collected by Anie"))
member("friends.blue_marble_counts", "jenny.marbles.blue.count", source("twice the number of blue marbles Jenny collected"))
member("friends.blue_marble_counts", "anie.marbles.blue.count", source("blue marbles collected by Anie"))
multiple(at("mary.marbles.red.count", "monday_to_friday"), at("jenny.marbles.red.count", "monday_to_friday"), 2, source("Mary collected twice as many red marbles as Jenny"))

fraction_of(at("mary.marbles.blue.count", "monday_to_friday"), at("anie.marbles.blue.count", "monday_to_friday"), 1, 2, source("Mary collected twice as many red marbles as Jenny and half the number of blue marbles collected by Anie"))
offset(at("anie.marbles.red.count", "monday_to_friday"), at("mary.marbles.red.count", "monday_to_friday"), 20, "count", source("Anie, who collected 20 more red marbles than Mary"))

multiple(at("anie.marbles.blue.count", "monday_to_friday"), at("jenny.marbles.blue.count", "monday_to_friday"), 2, source("Anie, who collected 20 more red marbles than Mary and twice the number of blue marbles Jenny collected"))
observe(at("jenny.marbles.red.count", "monday_to_friday"), 30, "count", source("Jenny collected 30 red marbles and 25 blue marbles"))
observe(at("jenny.marbles.blue.count", "monday_to_friday"), 25, "count", source("Jenny collected 30 red marbles and 25 blue marbles"))
query("sum", "friends.blue_marble_counts", "monday_to_friday")
assumptions: The stated marble counts and comparisons refer to totals over Monday through Friday.

f3_program: collection("claire.garden.flowers", "flower", "claire.garden", source("Claire has 400 flowers in her garden"))
collection("claire.garden.tulips", "tulip", "claire.garden", source("One hundred twenty are tulips"))
collection("claire.garden.roses", "rose", "claire.garden", source("the rest are roses"))
collection("claire.garden.roses.white", "rose", "claire.garden", source("Eighty of the roses are white"))
collection("claire.garden.roses.red", "rose", "claire.garden", source("the rest are red"))
observe(at("claire.garden.flowers.count", "initial"), 400, "count", source("Claire has 400 flowers in her garden"))
observe(at("claire.garden.tulips.count", "initial"), 120, "count", source("One hundred twenty are tulips"))

difference_relation(at("claire.garden.roses.count", "initial"), at("claire.garden.flowers.count", "initial"), at("claire.garden.tulips.count", "initial"), source("Claire has 400 flowers in her garden. One hundred twenty are tulips, and the rest are roses"))
observe(at("claire.garden.roses.white.count", "initial"), 80, "count", source("Eighty of the roses are white"))

difference_relation(at("claire.garden.roses.red.count", "initial"), at("claire.garden.roses.count", "initial"), at("claire.garden.roses.white.count", "initial"), source("Eighty of the roses are white, while the rest are red"))
observe(at("claire.garden.roses.red.unit_value", "current"), 0.75, "dollar_per_rose", source("Each red rose is worth $0.75"))

remove("sell_half_red_roses", "claire", at("claire.garden.roses.red.count", "current"), fraction(at("claire.garden.roses.red.count", "initial"), 1, 2), source("sell 1/2 of the total number of red roses"))

product_relation("claire.sale.earnings", at("claire.garden.roses.red.unit_value", "current"), event_field("sell_half_red_roses", "quantity"), source("Each red rose is worth $0.75. How much will Claire earn if she can sell 1/2 of the total number of red roses"))
query("value", "claire.sale.earnings")
assumptions: The sale occurs after the stated garden composition, so one-half refers to the pre-sale red-rose count.

f3_program: observe(at("group.financial_assets.fvpl.additions", "2019"), 44618, "RMB_million", cell("Additions (Note (a))", "2019"))
observe(at("group.financial_assets.fvpl.additions", "2018"), 60807, "RMB_million", cell("Additions (Note (a))", "2018"))
query("difference", at("group.financial_assets.fvpl.additions", "2018"), at("group.financial_assets.fvpl.additions", "2019"))
assumptions: Change is interpreted as the signed difference from 2018 to 2019.
